$comment: ★★★ ONE INLINE-ASM STATEMENT IS ONE INSTRUCTION WHILE REGISTERS ARE ALLOCATED, AND AN LL/SC PAIR UNDER PRESSURE TERMINATES (P68 round 8, D-LIR-ASM-TEMPLATE-SPILL-CODE-LANDS-BETWEEN-TEMPLATE-INSTRUCTIONS). Each shape runs with more values live around the statement than the target has registers, so the function spills: x86_64 — one statement naming 14 registers (13 inputs and an earlyclobber output), every input read again after it; aarch64 — the same with 29 registers, and an `ldaxr` / `add` / `stlxr` increment in ONE template, retried from C with 28 values live across it. Until the bundle each template line was its own allocation point and the allocator's spill and reload code landed BETWEEN them (✔MEASURED 2026-09-21: 29 instructions and 15 memory accesses inside a 7-line x86_64 template at release); a store between an `ldaxr` and its `stlxr` clears the exclusive monitor on every try. The retry is BOUNDED, so a pair that never succeeds exits 23 instead of hanging; 11/21 a sum read a wrong input, 22 the LL/SC result is wrong, 24 a value live across it changed. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 run it to 42 on x86_64 and on aarch64 (qemu), at -O0 and -O2. 29 registers in one aarch64 statement is within Mach-O's capacity too (x18 is platform-reserved there; 30 is refused by name, as by Apple's clang). ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: expand the bundle BEFORE allocation and the between-the-lines pin in `tests/lir/test_lir_asm_region.cpp` reddens; drop the target's `resultEarlyClobber` from `stlxr` and an overlap the programmer did not guard with `&` would encode — the status operands here carry `=&r`, as every correct LL/SC loop does.
